title: "Old Friend's Night Visit"
next_chapter_hook: "After Mo Xiansheng's figure vanished, the cracks on that ancient jade slip seemed to have grown deeper by another degree. Chen Ji knew that tonight was destined to be sleepless."

text.content: "The third quarter of the Hour of the Rat, inside Tianqing Sect Servants' Quarters. Chen Ji sat cross-legged on a worn-out meditation cushion, and between each breath of Tuna Breathing, the spiritual energy around him was so thin it could barely form a thread. The night wind outside the window wailed, causing the oil lamp to flicker unstably. This drafty broken room was the best disguise for his 'waste' of a body—no one cared about a Servant Disciple whose spiritual root was even deficient, and no one could have imagined that the Tianji Record Fragment was hidden in the jade pendant pressed against his body."

dialogue.content:
"'Chen Ji.'

An aged and hoarse voice suddenly rang within his Mental Sea. That voice seemed to pierce through from an extremely distant place, yet also seemed to whisper right by his ear, carrying an indescribable pressure.

'Tonight at the Hour of the Rat, at the Cliff in the Rear Mountain. I have urgent matters to discuss.'

The voice stopped abruptly, leaving no trace of its arrival or departure."

text.content: "Chen Ji's eyes snapped open, his pupils contracting sharply. The residual soul of Mo Xiansheng sealed on the first page of the Tianji Record had never taken the initiative to contact him. Unless... there was something that absolutely had to be said. He lowered his gaze, his fingertips gently stroking the hidden pattern on the jade pendant, calculations racing through his mind. This self-proclaimed guardian had been enigmatic from the very first scroll, often seeming about to speak yet stopping short. Today he appeared voluntarily—what on earth was his intention?"

"He rose and pushed open the wooden window. The cold wind carried the distinctive pine resin scent from the Rear Mountain, hitting him in the face. The distant Cliff was barely visible under the moonlight, like a crouching giant beast. That was the edge of the Sect's Forbidden Grounds—ordinary disciples would never dare venture there—but precisely because of that, it had become a perfect location for certain secret meetings. A faint cold smile curved Chen Ji's lips—Mo Xiansheng chose this place, and he understood his mindset well enough."

choice.prompt: "Mo Xiansheng invited him late at night, and Chen Ji decided to..."

choices.description: "Arrange perception formations around the meeting spot to ensure he has freedom to advance or retreat. Guard against any treachery from Mo Xiansheng."
choices.visible_cost: "Expend some mental energy to arrange formations"
choices.visible_reward: "Gain a tactical advantage, with the initiative in hand"
choices.risk_hint: "If noticed by Mo Xiansheng, it will expose his distrust"

text.content: "Hidden talisman techniques formed in Chen Ji's sleeves, and several unremarkable stones silently vanished into the night. He did not rise immediately; instead, he paced the room for a moment, memorizing the positions of several warning formations recorded in the Tianji Record Fragment. With everything prepared, beneath that seemingly calm face lay killing moves ready to strike back at any moment."

choices.description: "Since Mo Xiansheng holds the secrets of the Tianji Record, perhaps it is worth risking it once. Exchange more information through candor."
choices.visible_reward: "May win more trust from Mo Xiansheng"
choices.risk_hint: "If Mo Xiansheng harbors malicious intent, he will have no means to fight back"

text.content: "Chen Ji straightened his washed-out pale Taoist robe, took a deep breath, and pushed the door open. He chose to gamble—gamble that Mo Xiansheng still needed him at this moment. Under the moonlight, his back appeared especially frail, only those eyes occasionally flashing a sharpness entirely at odds with his 'waste' persona."

choices.text: "Use the Tianji Record to peer into tonight's trajectory"
choices.description: "First expend 5 points of Heavenly Fate, foresee the possible developments of tonight's meeting with Mo Xiansheng within the next three hours, then decide."
choices.visible_reward: "Obtain crucial information, avoid risks in advance"
choices.risk_hint: "Heavenly Fate expenditure is irreversible, and one may see images one does not wish to see"

text.content: "The Tianji Record Fragment within the jade pendant grew slightly warm. A profound power spread from his Brow Center. Amid flickering images, Chen Ji saw himself standing at the edge of the Cliff, yet Mo Xiansheng's phantom... was a blur. No matter how hard he tried, he could not see the true intentions behind that uncatchable face. This was the first time he encountered such strong interference in a divination—the feeling as if some force was deliberately obscuring Mo Xiansheng's identity."

"The Cliff in the Rear Mountain, the night wind sharp as a blade.

Chen Ji arrived silently among withered branches and fallen leaves, the moonlight stretching his gaunt figure long and thin. On a blue stone at the cliff's edge, a phantom figure stood with its back to him. That figure was shrouded in faint ink-colored mist, its outline ethereal and uncertain, as if it might dissipate in the wind at any moment. Mo Xiansheng's residual soul was indeed extraordinary."

dialogue.content:
"'You came.'

Mo Xiansheng did not turn around. That aged, hoarse voice echoed in the night wind, carrying a weariness of having traversed countless years.

'The old one has waited very long... so long that I almost forgot I was still alive.'"

"Chen Ji did not approach immediately, maintaining a distance of three zhang. His voice was平静得不起波澜 as he spoke:

'Mo Xiansheng summoned me late at night. Surely not for old times' sake. If there is something to say, please speak directly.'"

text.content:
"Mo Xiansheng finally turned around. It was an indescribable face—the features blurred like a reflection in water, yet only those two eyes were crystal clear, deep as if holding an entire galaxy. He looked at Chen Ji, and in that gaze there was even a trace of... pity?

'Directly?' Mo Xiansheng let out a low, hoarse laugh, 'Some words, once spoken, carry a price. Are you certain, truly certain you wish to hear?'"

choice.prompt: "Mo Xiansheng's words held hidden depths. How should Chen Ji respond?"

choices.text: "'Since the Master has already spoken, why bother testing?'"
choices.description: "Directly make his stance clear, refusing to play Mo Xiansheng's game of speaking in riddles. Force him to lay his cards on the table."
choices.visible_reward: "May force Mo Xiansheng to reveal more"
choices.risk_hint: "If Mo Xiansheng closes his mouth because of this, important information will be missed"

dialogue.content: "Mo Xiansheng was momentarily stunned, then let out a meaningful laugh: 'Good, very good. This child of yours is more like his ancestor than expected.' He clasped his hands behind his back, ink-colored mist surging around him. 'Since it is so, the old one shall ask you one thing—do you know, between you and me, precisely what is the relationship?'"

choices.text: "'Whatever the Master wishes to say, Chen Ji will listen.'"
choices.description: "Retreat to advance, giving Mo Xiansheng due respect, to see what he truly wishes to reveal."
choices.visible_reward: "Mo Xiansheng may take the initiative to reveal more hidden information"
choices.risk_hint: "May be led by the nose by Mo Xiansheng"

dialogue.content: "Mo Xiansheng nodded in satisfaction, the phantom drifting a step closer: 'A teachable child.' His voice suddenly grew somber. 'Chen Ji, have you ever considered—that every step you take, seemingly free, is actually upon an invisible chessboard?'"

choices.text: "'A price?' Chen Ji冷笑, 'What is the Master's price?'"
choices.description: "Defy conventional logic, counter-question Mo Xiansheng's stance. Test whether he is truly neutral."
choices.visible_reward: "May probe out Mo Xiansheng's true purpose"
choices.risk_hint: "Mo Xiansheng may become vigilant and stop revealing more"

dialogue.content: "Mo Xiansheng's phantom paused for a moment. In those deep eyes flashed a complex light: 'Well played, turning the tables.' He murmured softly, 'The old one's price? Merely that with each additional day lingering in this world, I watch one more day of the chess game.'"

text.content:
'Chess game.

This word appeared for the second time. Chen Ji firmly cataloged this detail in his mind, his expression betraying nothing. The night wind lifted the frayed hem of his robe. From the abyss beneath the Cliff came echoing sounds, as if some ancient behemoth breathed in its slumber. Mo Xiansheng simply watched him quietly, as if waiting for something."

dialogue.content:
"'What do you believe the Tianji Record to be?' Mo Xiansheng suddenly spoke, his voice carrying an indefinable tone. 'A divine artifact that foretells the future? A chance to defy fate and change destiny?'

He shook his head, ink-colored mist churning violently: 'It is merely a piece upon the chessboard. And you, Chen Ji...'

He paused, his gaze sharpening abruptly: 'You are the chosen chess player, and also... the piece destined to be sacrificed.'"

text.content: "Chen Ji's heart sank heavily, yet his face remained unruffled. Mo Xiansheng's words carried too much information—since the Tianji Record is a piece, who is the chess player? And what did this 'sacrificed piece' talk mean? He thought of the strange weakness he felt after every use of the Tianji Record, the images too blurred to see clearly, and a terrible suspicion quietly took shape in his heart."

"Mo Xiansheng seemed to see through his thoughts, his aged laughter echoing in the night wind: 'You're wondering who is manipulating all of this behind the scenes, aren't you?'

He stretched out a phantom hand, pointing to the heavens above: 'Look up at the sky. This heaven... it has eyes.'"

dialogue.content:
"Chen Ji did not look up. He knew what Mo Xiansheng was speaking of—the Eyes of Heavenly天道, that terrifying truth only revealed in the eighth scroll. But at this moment, he could not show any abnormality.

'The Master's chess game,' he said slowly, his voice terrifyingly calm, 'precisely what is it?'"

choice.prompt: "Mo Xiansheng's revelations deepen step by step. Chen Ji chooses to..."

choices.description: "Since he has already begun to speak, let him explain everything clearly this time. Even if some price must be paid, he must know it all."
choices.visible_reward: "May obtain the core secrets of the Tianji Record"
choices.risk_hint: "The risks are extremely high and unknown"

text.content: "No sooner had the words fallen than Mo Xiansheng's phantom shuddered violently. Those deep eyes flashed with genuine fear: 'Stop!' He hissed, his voice carrying true emotion for the first time, 'Some names must not be spoken lightly in this realm. If you insist on asking...' He closed his eyes, the phantom beginning to distort intensely, 'Enough, enough. This conversation ends here today.'"

result_nodes.description: "Mo Xiansheng has revealed too much already. First digest this information, do not stir up trouble."
result_nodes.visible_cost: "May miss the chance for deeper understanding"
result_nodes.visible_reward: "Preserve strength, do not expose trump cards"

text.content: "Chen Ji lowered his gaze, assuming a thoughtful expression. Mo Xiansheng, upon seeing this, nodded slightly: 'You are more composed than the old one imagined.' The phantom stabilized once more, the distortion fading into nothing. 'Remember every word from tonight. When you are ready, we shall speak again.'"

result_nodes.text: "Lob a probing question: 'Which numbered piece is the Master?'"
result_nodes.description: "Since we are all pieces, let's see how much this old fellow knows. Also test his true relationship with the Tianji Record."
result_nodes.visible_reward: "May probe out Mo Xiansheng's true identity"
result_nodes.risk_hint: "Mo Xiansheng's reaction will determine the trajectory of their future relationship"

dialogue.content:
"Mo Xiansheng was stunned.

In those deep eyes, rarely, a most complex expression appeared—bitterness, relief, and even a trace of... respect?

'Well... which numbered piece.' He repeated softly, his voice carrying the weight of years, 'The old one's number, I no longer remember. But remember this—every generation of Tianji Record inheritor is the grave-digger of the previous one.'"

text.content:
"Every generation of Tianji Record inheritor is the grave-digger of the previous one.

This sentence poured over Chen Ji like a basin of ice water. He remembered that in the first scroll, Mo Xiansheng had called himself the 'Chessboard Guardian'—guarding the chessboard, not guarding him Chen Ji. Then, what exactly was he guarding? Was he waiting for the next inheritor to fulfill the mission of ending the previous one?"

dialogue.content:
"'Whatever you are thinking, the old one sees it clearly.' Mo Xiansheng's voice broke his thoughts. 'But there is one thing you must understand—the old one is different from those lofty chess players.'

He paused, the phantom actually bowing slightly: 'Chen Xuan chose you back then. The old one is your protector, not your executioner. This point... has never changed.'"

text.content: "Chen Ji did not respond. The night wind grew increasingly biting, almost blinding him, yet he remained motionless, standing his ground in that stare-down with the phantom figure. Mo Xiansheng said he was different from those chess players—but who could say this wasn't just another form of rhetoric? In this chess game of destiny, who could truly be trusted?"

dialogue.content:
"'Enough. Tonight, too much has been said.' Mo Xiansheng suddenly spoke, the phantom beginning to fade gradually. 'Before we part, the old one will give you one final piece of advice—'

His voice grew ever more distant, yet each word rang clear:

'Within the chess game, the only freedom is choosing when to make your move. As for where it falls...'

He cast one final glance at Chen Ji, that gaze carrying a rare hint of tenderness: 'When you truly wish to win, you will know naturally.'"

text.content:
"The ink-colored mist dissipated completely. On the Cliff stood only Chen Ji alone.

He stood alone beneath the moonlight, gazing up at that profound night sky. The preceding conversation was like a key, unlocking a door long sealed shut—behind it lay an even more complex situation, deeper conspiracies, and... a truth he had never imagined.

Eyes of Heavenly天道, the chess game of destiny, the sacrificed pieces of every generation...

He suddenly thought of his sister Chen Nian's face. That figure forever blurred in the Tianji Record's visions—her existence, was it coincidence, or another variable?"

"Chen Ji collected his thoughts and turned to walk back the way he came. The moonlight stretched his back long and thin. Beneath that calm face churned an unending tempest.

The information Mo Xiansheng revealed tonight, he had already memorized completely. Chess game, sacrificed pieces, Eyes of Heavenly天道... these keywords, like scattered puzzle pieces, were slowly assembling into a shocking picture within his mind.

But what concerned him most was Mo Xiansheng's final glance before departing—that was unmistakably... the gaze one gives a person already marked for death."

"Returning to the Servants' Quarters, Chen Ji did not rest immediately. He lit the nearly-exhausted oil lamp and retrieved the Tianji Record Fragment from his chest. The cracks on the jade slip had grown deeper than yesterday—this was the mark of Heavenly Fate draining away. He stared at that crack for a long while, then suddenly laughed softly: 'Sacrificed piece, is it...'

He returned the fragment to his chest and closed his eyes. Tomorrow there were still many things to do—Su Qingyao's investigation continued, and the Holy Sect's movements required attention. And that so-called chess game of destiny...

Someday, he would overturn this entire game."

"Outside the window the night wind gradually subsided. The east horizon faintly brightened with the first pale light of dawn.

Chen Ji lay on that creaking wooden bed, gazing at the drafty roof, his mind repeatedly replaying Mo Xiansheng's final words—'When you truly wish to win, you will know naturally.'

Wish to win?

He suddenly realized—had everything he had done so carefully, his every cautious stratagem, truly been merely to 'win'? Or had he simply been desperately struggling, trying to escape a destiny already written?

Regardless, tonight's conversation taught him one thing—from the moment he obtained the Tianji Record, he had entered the game. And the stakes of this chess game were his life, and the lives of everyone he cared about."
